unit.title: Exploring Measures
unit.blurb: Area and perimeter of rectangles, compound shapes and right-angled triangles, and working with time, including the 24-hour clock and timetables.
unit.subject: maths

O1.t: Find the area and perimeter of rectangles and compound shapes, and the area of right-angled triangles.

O2.t: Use 12- and 24-hour clocks, convert between units of time and find time intervals, including with timetables.

p: The **perimeter** is the distance all the way round. The **area** is the space inside, measured in square units such as **cm²**.
For a rectangle: **area = length × width** and perimeter = 2 × (length + width).
A right-angled triangle is **half a rectangle**. Area = (base × height) ÷ 2.
Split an L-shape into two rectangles, find each area, then add.

lesson.t: Why a triangle is half a rectangle
p: Draw a rectangle around a right-angled triangle: the triangle is exactly half of it. So the area of a triangle is half of base × height.
Area is measured in square units (cm²) because it counts squares.

lesson.q: A triangle has a base of 8 cm and a height of 5 cm. Find its area.
steps: half of the rectangle around it

p: Find the base and the perpendicular height.
Perimeter is a length (cm); area is measured in square units (cm²).

p: The 24-hour clock counts hours from 00:00 (midnight) to 23:59. Afternoon times add 12: 3:45 p.m. = **15:45**.
1 hour = 60 minutes, 1 minute = 60 seconds, 1 day = 24 hours.
Count on in steps: from 09:45 to 11:20 → 15 minutes to 10:00, 1 hour to 11:00, 20 minutes to 11:20: **1 hour 35 minutes**.
The 24-hour clock avoids a.m. and p.m. mistakes. Times after midday have hours from 13 to 23.

lesson.q: A trip starts at 10:50 and ends at 14:15. How long is it?

p: Count on to the next hour.
Count on to the end and add.
Time does not work in hundreds: 1:50 + 20 minutes is 2:10, not 1:70.
